newsitem.title: USA: Writer Patricia Cornwell admits lesbian affair. [CORRECTED 21:20 GMT].
newsitem.headline: Writer Patricia Cornwell admits lesbian affair. [CORRECTED 21:20 GMT].

text.p: After a year denying it, bestselling mystery writer Patricia Cornwell has admitted she had a lesbian affair with a former FBI agent involved in a sensational court case, Vanity Fair magazine said on Tuesday.

Vanity Fair reporter Judy Bachrach said Cornwell told her in an interview "I'm gonna go for broke with you" and said she had a a brief affair with Margo Bennett, whose husband Gene was convicted in February in Manassas, Virginia, of trying to murder his ex-wife after claiming to be enraged by the affair.

"It wasn't even two trips over the rug, as we say here .... it was very brief in every way you can imagine," Vanity Fair quoted Cornwell as saying in her Richmond, Virginia, home about an affair that began in 1991 and ended the next year.
Bachrach said Cornwell had previously been reluctant to discuss the allegations of lesbianism that were aired during Gene Bennett's trial that ended with the jury recommending a 61-year sentence.
Cornwell, one of the world's best-paid female writers, told the London Sunday Times last year she wished the allegations were true, "because maybe then my life would be more interesting."

Bennett was convicted of luring his wife to a Manassas church, taking the pastor hostage at gunpoint and finally fleeing after his wife, like her husband an ex-FBI agent, shot at him with a gun she had brought for her protection.
Vanity Fair said one reason for Bennett's actions was revealed in the couple's divorce papers in which he charged that his wife had been having an affair with Cornwell.

The magazine said Cornwell, 40, also discussed other aspects of her life including past fights against manic-depression, anorexia, bulimia and excessive drinking, which she now claims to have conquered.

It also said Cornwell had made an unsuccessful bid to lure actress Jodie Foster into playing her detective character Kay Scarpetta in a film version of one of her books. The effort included Cornwell's seeking out Foster's childhood tutor and trying to convince her to make an introduction.
(Corrects spelling of Foster's first name from Jody).
When the woman took ill, Cornwell hung around the hospital hoping to run into Foster. But when the two finally met, Foster declined the offer.

Actress Demi Moore also declined the role because Cornwell failed to show her a completed script. Cornwell complained "the courtship's over" even though the two had "sat in hot tubs and smoked cigars," according to Vanity Fair.
